title: Navigation & Orientation
description: Learn how to find your way around the filesystem.

levels.title: Where am I? — pwd
levels.lesson:
Every command you run happens inside a directory — a folder on the filesystem. Before you can do anything useful, you need to know where you are.

`pwd` stands for **print working directory**. It prints the full path of the directory you're currently inside. Run it any time you feel lost.

challenge.instruction: Run `pwd` to see your current directory.

levels.title: What's here? — ls
levels.lesson:
`ls` lists the contents of a directory — the files and folders inside it.

With no arguments it shows what's in your **current** directory. You can also give it a path to peek into any other directory without moving there:

```
ls /etc
```

Items shown are sorted alphabetically.

challenge.instruction: Run `ls` to list the contents of your current directory.

levels.title: Hidden files — ls -a
levels.lesson:
Files and directories whose names start with `.` are **hidden** — `ls` skips them by default. Hidden files are typically configuration files you rarely need to touch directly (`.bashrc`, `.gitconfig`, etc.).

The `-a` flag tells `ls` to show **all** entries, including hidden ones.

```
ls -a
```

You'll also see `.` (the current directory itself) and `..` (its parent) — those are always present.

challenge.instruction: Run `ls -a` to reveal hidden files in your current directory.

levels.title: Moving around — cd
levels.lesson:
`cd` (**change directory**) moves you into a different directory.

You can use an **absolute path** (starting with `/`, always from the root) or a **relative path** (from wherever you are right now):

```
cd /home/user/Documents   # absolute — works from anywhere
cd Documents              # relative — works if you're in /home/user
cd ..                     # go up one level
cd                        # no argument = go home (~)
```

levels.title: Checkpoint — Navigation
levels.lesson:
Time to combine what you've learned. Checkpoints test several skills at once — there's no single right command, just a final state you need to reach.

Skills covered: `cd`, `ls`, `pwd`.

challenge.instruction: Navigate to `/var/log`, then run `ls` to see what's there.
